messages:
rebecca-sales: Hydrangea Therapeutics wants a focused POC next week. Requirements: sustained 300 qps, mixed workload (search-like short prompts + long generation), p95/p99 targets, coldstart behavior, and CMK for embedding storage. Need a short runbook and a 12mo dedicated quote + 1mo hosted PoC price.

omar-eng: Mixed workload changes batching profile. What's the split short vs long?

rebecca-sales: They provided a mix: 60% short (<=40 tokens in, 30 tokens out), 40% long (avg 420 in, 250 out). Session reuse ~65%.

omar-eng: That shifts tokens/s: at 300 qps combined tokens ~300*(0.6*(40+30)+0.4*(420+250)) = ~300*(42+268) = ~300*310 = 93k tok/s. Prefix caching still helps for sessions. For mixed tails, we should separate request classes in the generator and measure per-class p95/p99.

sylvie-ops: Draft runbook idea: two isolated traffic slices (short/long) routed via same pool but tagged so we can get per-class metrics. 30m steady @300 qps, 10m interleaved bursts (short-heavy then long-heavy), and 6 coldstart cycles including an angry-burst immediately after restart. Include KMS rotation mid-run.

david-sre: For tail SLOs, recommend continuous batching cap=18ms, KV cache enabled, and per-session routing to keep cache hit rates high. Also recommend multi-AZ nodes and a pre-warmed standby to reduce coldstarts for long requests.

tara-qa: I'll build the harness with per-class histograms. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 per class, tokens/s, model queue length, GPU util, coldstart warmup time, and KMS call latencies. Also test model-fallback: route long requests to a slightly smaller variant if latency breaches SLO for >90s.

rebecca-sales: Hydrangea asked about cost sensitivity if they lower max context to 512 from 2048 and/or use 4-bit quant. Any quick numbers?

omar-eng: Rough sensitivity: lowering context to 512 reduces token work for long requests by ~60% (so effective GPUs drop by ~40% for the long slice). 4-bit quant can improve throughput ~1.6x vs 8-bit, so combined could cut GPUs needed from ~8-9 down to ~4-5 for Dedicated. We'll include a small sensitivity table.

sylvie-ops: Preliminary ballparks: Dedicated reserved (8 GPUs steady target, autoscale 5-12): "$63k/month" (compute+infra+support). Hosted PoC (1mo, managed, logs & sampling): "$20k". Marked as preliminary.

david-sre: KMS note: kms-bot: "CMK STATUS: Customer-managed CMK supported on Dedicated and Private planes. Hosted plane supports envelope encryption; for CMK in-path with minimal latency recommend Dedicated in same VPC. Expect synchronous CMK calls to add ~8-18ms depending on placement; in-VPC ~4-8ms."

rebecca-sales: Procurement will ask about key rotation impact on throughput. Can we simulate rotation and show results?

tara-qa: Yes  we'll trigger rotation at minute 22 and measure embedding latencies and end-to-end p95. Also run an async DEK variation to compare.

omar-eng: We'll also include a hosted control run so they can see delta on tail latency and unit cost. Hosted will likely have slightly higher p95 on long requests due to noisier multitenant tails.

sylvie-ops: Ops fallback and playbook: keep 1 pre-warmed node per AZ for long requests; autoscale by token/s and queue latency; fallback to smaller model variant and enable circuit-breaker to preserve SLOs. Add a short-run RTO for keys rolling (grace period).

rebecca-sales: Timeline: runbook draft by Mon EOD, infra ready Tue, POC Wed-Thu, analysis Fri. Tara, can you post the one-pager exec summary with per-class p50/p95/p99, tokens/M cost, recommended commit, KMS impact and mitigations?

tara-qa: Will do. Also will include a short appendix with the harness commands and a sample traffic config.

rebecca-sales: Awesome. One last ask from their CTO: what happens to tail latency if KMS is unavailable for 15s? Any automatic fallback?

david-sre: If synchronous KMS is on the critical path we will see a spike; ops can configure short-circuit using cached DEKs for a configured TTL to tolerate KMS unavailability for short windows. We'll demonstrate that in the run by disabling KMS for 15s at minute 28 and showing the cached-DEK behavior.

kms-bot: "OP NOTE: cached DEK support available; when enabled, fallback window default TTL=30s (configurable). Recommend testing with TTL=60s for sensitive workloads."

rebecca-sales: Great. I'll send this plan to Hydrangea and schedule the security sync. Ping this thread when results are posted. :rocket:
